STUDYQURAN:86:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:8/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:86:8/r1.claim: As in 19:67 and 22:5, the Quran argues that the One who creates humans from dust and then a drop can surely resurrect them, as 30:27 says this is most easy for Him.
STUDYQURAN:86:8/r1.anchor: if God is able to create human beings from dust, then from a drop (35:11), then He can surely resurrect them, as in 30:27

STUDYQURAN:86:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:8/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:86:8/r2.claim: Many pre-Islamic Arabs accepted God as Creator but did not accept that He could resurrect the dead.
STUDYQURAN:86:8/r2.anchor: Many pre-Islamic Arabs accepted that God was the Creator, but did not accept that He could resurrect the dead

TAB-FULL:v24p297/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r1.claim: God who made people from emitted fluid and fashioned them as sound humans is able to return them; the reports differ over what the pronoun in رجعه denotes.
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: " {إنه على رجعه لقادر} [الطارق: 8] قال: إنه على رده في صلبه لقادر "

TAB-FULL:v24p297/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r2.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r2.claim: One group takes the pronoun to refer to water, meaning God can return semen to the place from which it emerged.
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: " {إنه على رجعه لقادر} [الطارق: 8] قال: إنه على رده في صلبه لقادر "

TAB-FULL:v24p297/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r3.claim: Ikrima says God can return the fluid to the backbone.
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: " {إنه على رجعه لقادر} [الطارق: 8] قال: إنه على رده في صلبه لقادر "

TAB-FULL:v24p297/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r4.claim: Mujahid says God can return the emitted fluid to the urethra; he repeats this interpretation in several reports.
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {إنه على رجعه لقادر} [الطارق: 8] قال: على أن يرد الماء في الإحليل "

TAB-FULL:v24p297/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets this as God's ability to return the human to water as he was before being created.
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {إنه على رجعه لقادر} [الطارق: 8] إن شئت رددته كما خلقته من ماء "

TAB-FULL:v24p297/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says God can hold back the fluid so it does not emerge, just as He was able to create from it.
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {إنه على رجعه لقادر}

TAB-FULL:v24p297/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r7.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r7.claim: Other interpreters say the verse means God can return a person from old age to youth.
TAB-FULL:v24p297/r7.anchor: من حال الكبر إلى حال الصغر

TAB-FULL:v24p299/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God can reverse a person's life stages, restoring him from old age through youth and childhood to semen.
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r1.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان، عن الضحاك، قال: سمعته يقول

TAB-FULL:v24p299/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r2.claim: Qatāda interprets the return as God's ability to resurrect and restore the human after death.
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r2.anchor: ثنا يزيد، قال: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة

TAB-FULL:v24p299/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers resurrection: the next verse's Day when secrets are tested makes the return a resurrection event, with that Day qualifying when God restores the dead alive as before.
TAB-FULL:v24p299/r3.anchor: فكان في إتباعه قوله {إنه على رجعه لقادر} [الطارق: 8] نبأ من أنباء القيامة

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.claim: The Angel of Death takes people at death, and God takes souls at death and sleep; angelic preservation can also mean preserving souls through writing their deeds.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r1.anchor: ولا ينافي هذا الوجه ظاهر آية الانفطار السابقة من أن حفظ الملائكة هو الكتابة

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.claim: An objection says absolute power cannot prove resurrection because recreating the very same human is impossible: a second body would be merely like, not identical to, the first.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r2.anchor: ومحصله أن إطلاق القدرة إنما ينفع فيما كان ممكنا لكن إعادة الإنسان بعينه محال فإن الإنسان المخلوق ثانيا مثل الانسان الدنيوي

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.claim: The answer is that personal identity resides in the preserved soul, not the body; when that soul joins a recreated body, it is the same person despite bodily similarity.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r3.anchor: وجه الاندفاع أن شخصية الشخص من الإنسان بنفسه لا ببدنه والنفس محفوظة فإذا خلق البدن وتعلقت به النفس كان هو الإنسان الدنيوي بشخصه

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r8.claim: The return is resurrection; the pronoun refers to God, whose identity is obvious enough that the text does not name Him explicitly.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r8.anchor: له تعالى واكتفى بالإضمار مع أن المقام مقام الإظهار لظهوره

TABATABAI:86:5-9/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r9.claim: The one who created a human from such water can restore him after death; resurrection is like the beginning, and power over a thing entails power over its like.
TABATABAI:86:5-9/r9.anchor: لقادر لأن القدرة على الشيء قدرة على مثله إذ حكم الأمثال فيما يجوز وفيما لا يجوز واحد

TABRISI:86:2-9/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:2-9/r16.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والجبائي
TABRISI:86:2-9/r16.claim: The author prefers the explanation that God can resurrect a person after death, since the following verse speaks of the day hidden things are tested.
TABRISI:86:2-9/r16.anchor: يعني أن الذي خلقه ابتداء من هذا الماء يقدر على أن يرجعه حيا بعد الموت عن الحسن وقتادة والجبائي

TABRISI:86:2-9/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:2-9/r17.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
TABRISI:86:2-9/r17.claim: An alternative says God can return the fluid to the backbone.
TABRISI:86:2-9/r17.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنه تعالى على رد الماء في الصلب لقادر عن عكرمة ومجاهد

TABRISI:86:2-9/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:2-9/r18.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:86:2-9/r18.claim: Another view says God can return the person to fluid as before.
TABRISI:86:2-9/r18.anchor: وقيل: إنه على رد الإنسان ماء كما كان قادر عن الضحاك

TABRISI:86:2-9/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:2-9/r19.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
TABRISI:86:2-9/r19.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan interprets the return as God’s ability to reverse the person’s life stages from old age through youth and childhood back to semen.
TABRISI:86:2-9/r19.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: يقول إن شئت رددته من الكبر إلى الشباب ومن الشباب إلى الصبى

THALABI:v10p179/r23.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r23.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p179/r23.claim: Qatada says God is able to resurrect a person and return him after death.
THALABI:v10p179/r23.anchor: قال قتادة: إن الله سبحانه على بعث الإنسان وإعادته بعد الموت قادر

THALABI:v10p179/r24.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r24.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v10p179/r24.claim: Ikrima interprets the return as God’s ability to restore the water to the loins from which it came.
THALABI:v10p179/r24.anchor: وقال عكرمة: إن الله سبحانه على رد الماء إلى الصلب الذي خرج منه لقادر

THALABI:v10p179/r25.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r25.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v10p179/r25.claim: Mujahid says God can return the semen into the urethra.
THALABI:v10p179/r25.anchor: وعن مجاهد: على رد النطفة في الإحليل، وعن الضحاك: إنه على رد الإنسان ماء

THALABI:v10p179/r26.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r26.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v10p179/r26.claim: Al-Dahhak says God can restore a person to the state of water he was in before.
THALABI:v10p179/r26.anchor: وعن الضحاك: إنه على رد الإنسان ماء كما كان قبل لقادر، مقاتل بن حيان عنه: يقول

THALABI:v10p179/r27.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r27.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
THALABI:v10p179/r27.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says God can reverse a person’s development from old age to youth, childhood, and finally semen.
THALABI:v10p179/r27.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان عنه: يقول: إن شئت رددته من الكبر إلى الشباب ومن الشباب إلى الصبى

THALABI:v10p179/r28.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p179/r28.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p179/r28.claim: Ibn Zayd says God is able to hold back the water so that it does not emerge.
THALABI:v10p179/r28.anchor: وعن ابن زيد: أنه على حبس ذلك الماء لقادر حتى لا يخرج

BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.claim: Creation from matter untouched by life proves the Creator can restore the dead, indeed more readily by rational analogy, so people should prepare for recompense.
BURSEVI:v10p309/r4.anchor: من قدر على إنشائه من مواد لم تشم رائحة الحياة قط فهو قادر على إعادته بل أقدر على قياس العقل

BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r9.claim: The pronoun in “indeed He” refers to the Creator, indicated by the preceding statement that He created.
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r9.anchor: إنه} الضمير للخالق فإن قوله خلق يدل عليه

BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r10.claim: The Creator who first made the human from the described matter can restore him after death, with no deficiency of power.
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r10.anchor: إن ذلك الذي خلق الإنسان ابتداء مما ذكر {على رجعه} أي إعادته بعد موته {لقادر} أي لبين القدرة بحيثلا يرى له عجز أصلا

BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r11.claim: Placing “upon his return” before “is able” emphasizes the specific subject under discussion and does not restrict God’s ability to other acts.
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r11.anchor: وتقديم الجار والمجرور على عامله وهو لقادر للاهتمام به من حيث إن الكلام فيه بخصوصه

BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r12.claim: Some say God created to display power, provided sustenance to display generosity, caused death to display omnipotence, and resurrects to manifest reward and punishment.
BURSEVI:v10p309#2/r12.anchor: قال بعضهم : خلقه لإظهار قدرته ثم رزقه لإظهار الكرم ثم يميته لإظهار الجبروت ثم يحييه لإظهار الثواب والعقاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p413/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p413/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p413/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the return is the water's being returned to the urethra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p413/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: على أن يرد الماء في الإحليل (¬3) (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p413/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p413/r2.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p413/r2.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the return is the water's being returned to the loins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p413/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة (¬5)، (والضحاك) (¬6) (¬7): على أن يرد الماء في الصلب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:86:1-8/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:86:1-8/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:86:1-8/r5.claim: God is able to resurrect and restore the human after death.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:86:1-8/r5.anchor: { إنه } إن الله { على رجعه } على بعث الإنسان وإعادته بعد الموت { لقادر }.

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.claim: A creation account in al-Muʾminūn lists nine stages: clay extract, drop, clinging form, lump, bones, flesh, new creation, death, and resurrection.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r13.anchor: birincisi “sülâletin min tîn”, ikincisi “nutfe”, üçüncüsü “aleka”, dördüncüsü “mudga”, beşincisi “izâm”, altıncısı “lahm”, yedincisi “halk-ı âhar”, sekizinci “mevt”, dokuzuncusu “ba‘s”tir

ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.claim: These verses condense the stages to recall God's preservation and power to resurrect; they begin with the most evident and immediate starting point for reflection, the spurting fluid.
ELMALILI:86:5-7#2/r14.anchor: bütün o merâtib مِمَّ خُلِقَ خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍۢ دَافِقٍۢ يَخْرُجُ مِنۢ بَيْنِ ٱلصُّلْبِ وَٱلتَّرَآئِبِ إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِۦ لَقَادِرٌۭ mazmunlarında hulâsa edilerek

ELMALILI:86:8-10/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r1.claim: The Creator who first formed the human being can return him through death and resurrection, bringing him before God and making Himself known.
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r1.anchor: Şüphesiz o yaradan o insanı döndürmeye elbette kādirdir

ELMALILI:86:8-10/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r2.claim: This return expresses the Qur’anic teaching that people return to God, which Elmalılı connects to 2:245, 10:56, 11:34, 28:70–88, 36:22–83, 41:21, and 43:85.
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r2.anchor: mazmûnunu ifade eden bu ircâ‘insanın Sûre-i Mü’minûn’da zikrolunan dokuz tavrından

ELMALILI:86:8-10/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r3.claim: Elmalılı identifies the return as the eighth and ninth of the nine human stages in al-Mu’minun: death followed by resurrection on Judgment Day.
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r3.anchor: insanın Sûre-i Mü’minûn’da zikrolunan dokuz tavrından sekizinci ve dokuzuncu mertebe olarak

ELMALILI:86:8-10/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r11.claim: “The day when secrets are tested” modifies the return, not “is able”; God’s power is unrestricted by that day, so Elmalılı prefers treating it as a new sentence.
ELMALILI:86:8-10/r11.anchor: Bu yevm ilk nazarda zannedilebileceği gibi “kādir”in zarfı değil, “rec‘”e müte‘alliktir, çünkü kudret o gün ile mukayyed değil

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.claim: Those denying resurrection and the afterlife are urged to learn from their own creation and judge whether resurrection after death is possible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r1.anchor: Öldükten sonra dirilmeyi ve âhiret hayatını inkâr eden insanın, kendi yaratılışına bakarak ibret alması ve öldükten sonra yeniden dirilmeyi (ba‘s), dolayısıyla âhiret gerçeğini buna göre değerlendirmesi istenmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r7.claim: The Creator who made humans from fluid and formed them perfectly is emphatically able to raise them after death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:5/r7.anchor: insanı yukarıda anlatıldığı şekilde meniden yaratıp mükemmel bir varlık haline getiren yüce yaratıcının onu öldükten sonra diriltmeye de kadir olduğu vurgulu bir şekilde ifade edilmektedir

QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r10.claim: God is able to resurrect and recreate the human being.
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r10.anchor: إنه على بعثه ، وخلقه مرة أخرى لقادر

QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r11.claim: Since God's power is perfect, power over a thing entails power over its like, and resurrection is equivalent in meaning to origination.
QUSHAYRI:v3p412/r11.anchor: والقدرة على الشيء تقتضي القدرة على مثله ، والإعادة في معنى الابتداء

BURHAN:v1p309/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p309/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p309/r1.claim: In 86:8, يوم semantically belongs with the verbal noun رجعه, but syntax bars separating that noun from its complement with an unrelated element, so an implied verb governs يوم.
BURHAN:v1p309/r1.anchor: لكن الإعراب يمنع منه لعدم جواز الفصل بين المصدر ومعموله بأجنبى

ITQAN:v2p535#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p535#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p535#2/r1.claim: Meaning would attach “on the day secrets are tested” to the verbal noun “return,” but syntax bars separating a verbal noun from its complement; an implicit verb indicated by “return” is supplied.
ITQAN:v2p535#2/r1.anchor: فالظرف الذي هو يوم يقتضي المعنى أنه يتعلق بالمصدر وهو رجع أي أنه على رجعه في ذلك اليوم لقادر

DAMGHANI:v1p434/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p434/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p434/r10.claim: The entry also lists guidance, passing, and literal walking as other senses of mashā, without elaboration in this excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p434/r10.anchor: م ش ى على أربعة أوجه المضى . الهدى . المر . المشى بعينه

FARRA:v3p254#2/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p254#2/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p254#2/r11.claim: God is able to return the human being after death.
FARRA:v3p254#2/r11.anchor: إنه على رد الإنسان بعد الموت لقادر

FARRA:v3p254#2/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p254#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
FARRA:v3p254#2/r12.claim: Mujāhid interprets the return as returning the fluid to the urethra.
FARRA:v3p254#2/r12.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: إنه على رد الماء إلى الإحليل لقادر

NAHHAS:v5p199/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r1.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p199/r1.claim: Qatada takes the pronoun to refer to the human and رجعه to mean resurrecting him; al-Nahhas calls this the clearest view, also chosen by Muhammad ibn Jarir.
NAHHAS:v5p199/r1.anchor: فمن أصح ما قيل فيه قول قتادة قال على بعثه وإعادته فالضمير على هذا للإنسان

NAHHAS:v5p199/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r2.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v5p199/r2.claim: Mujahid says رجعه means returning the semen to the urethra.
NAHHAS:v5p199/r2.anchor: عن ليث عن مجاهد ( إنه على رجعه لقادر ) قال على رد الماء في الإحليل

NAHHAS:v5p199/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v5p199/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd takes رجعه as God’s ability to hold the fluid back so it does not emerge.
NAHHAS:v5p199/r3.anchor: وهو مذهب ابن زيد قال على رجعه لقادر على حبسه حتى لا يخرج

NAHHAS:v5p199/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r4.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v5p199/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak gives a gloss like the two explanations about returning or withholding the fluid.

NAHHAS:v5p199/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r5.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v5p199/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak also says God can return a person through the stages of life in reverse, from old age to youth, youth to childhood, and childhood to semen.
NAHHAS:v5p199/r5.anchor: وعنه قول ثالث على رجعه لقادر قال على رجعه بعد الكبر إلى الشباب وبعد الشباب إلى الصبا وبعد الصبا إلى النطفة

NAHHAS:v5p199/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p199/r6.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects Muhammad ibn Jarir’s claim that يوم تبلى السرائر attaches to رجعه: that would split a relative construction from its antecedent with إن’s predicate; يوم instead governs ناصر.
NAHHAS:v5p199/r6.anchor: هي خطأ في العربية زعم أن قوله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the Creator, indicated by خلق; it is known that no one else creates.
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r1.anchor: الضمير للخالق المدلول عليه بقوله: " خلق " لأنه معلوم أن لا خالق سواه

SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r2.claim: The ه in رجعه may refer to the human being, meaning God's power to resurrect him after death.
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r2.anchor: في الهاء وجهان، أحدهما: أنه ضمير الإنسان، أي: على بعثه بعد موته

SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r3.claim: Alternatively, ه refers to the water: semen returns into the urethra or the backbone.
SAMIN-DURR:86:8/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه ضمير الماء، أي: يرجع المني في الإحليل أو الصلب

ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r7.claim: One tafsīr explanation takes the return as the water's return to the urethra.
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r7.anchor: جاء في التفسير: على رجع الماء إلى الإحليل لقادر

ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r8.claim: Another explanation takes the return as the water's return to the loins.
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r8.anchor: وجاء أيضا على رجعه إلى الصلب

ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r9.claim: He favors the interpretation that God can resurrect the human, supported by the mention of the day secrets are tested.
ZAJJAJ:v5p311#2/r9.anchor: وجاء أيضا على رجعه على بعث الإنسان

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.claim: Human origin is a bodily fluid, not a rare substance beyond God's reach; since He made a living person from it, He can recreate him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r5.anchor: he is made from a drop of fluid which emanates from his own body.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p450/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p450/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p450/r9.claim: The oath’s response may be the clause governed by إن in any form; another view takes إنه على رجعه لقادر as the response and the intervening text as parenthetical.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p450/r9.anchor: وجواب القسم هو ما دخلت عليه إن، سواء كانت المخففة أو المشددة أو النافية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the Creator implied by خلق.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r1.anchor: إنه: الضمير يعود على الخالق الدال عليه خلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r2.claim: They take the pronoun to refer to the human restored to life after death; Abū Ḥayyān calls this the stronger view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة: الضمير في رجعه عائد على الإنسان، أي على رده حيا بعد موته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r3.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it means returning a person from old age to youth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: على رده من الكبر إلى الشباب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r4.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r4.claim: They take the pronoun to refer to fluid returned to the urethra or backbone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومجاهد: الضمير عائد على الماء، أي على رد الماء في الإحليل أو في الصلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says grammarians avoid making لقادر the governor lest power seem limited to that day; Abū Ḥayyān replies that power is universal but Judgment is singled out as the crucial warning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وكل هذه الفرق فرت من أن يكون العامل لقادر، لأنه يظهر من ذلك تخصيص القدرة في ذلك اليوم وحده

ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r1.claim: The first pronoun refers to God the Creator; leaving the agent unspoken in the earlier creation statement magnifies Him as its sole possible referent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r1.anchor: الضمير الأول للخالق تعالى شأنهوكما فخم أولا بترك الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r2.claim: The second pronoun refers to the human being: the One who first created him from this fluid can clearly restore him after death.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r2.anchor: والضمير الثاني للإنسان أي إن ذلك الذي خلقه ابتداء مما ذكر على إعادته بعد موته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r3.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashshaf glosses the emphatic capable as clearly powerful; Alusi says the argument particularly targets resurrection, leaving other divine capabilities aside for this purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r3.anchor: ولذا فسر قادر هنا يبين القدرة كما في الكشاف واعتبر فيه الأختصاص فقال أي على إعادته خصوصا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r4.claim: The wording is emphatic because the proof is already clear; the sentence stands apart as the answer to the implied question.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r4.anchor: فصل الجملة عما سبق لكونه جواب الأستفهام دونها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r5.claim: The prepositional phrase may attach directly to capable or be understood through the relative pronoun governed by it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r5.anchor: وحينئذ يراد ما ذكر جعل الجار من صلة لقادر أو مدلولا على موصوله به على المذهبين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r6.claim: Mujahid and Ikrima take the pronoun to mean the fluid, so God returns it to the urethra or the loins; Alusi rejects this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة الضمير الثاني للماء أي أنه تعالى على رد الماء في الأحليل أو في الصلب لقادر وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that the pronoun means returning a person from old age to youth; Alusi says this interpretation is likewise unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r7.anchor: ومثله كون المعنى على تقدير كونه للإنسان أنه وجل على رده من الكبر إلى الشباب لقادر كما روي عن الضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the principal interpretation that God can restore the human being after death.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p98#2/r8.anchor: وما ذكرناه أولا مروي عن ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the return is restoring the semen to the urethra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: على رد النطفة في الإحليل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says it is restoring the fluid to the loins from which it came.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة: على رد الماء في الصلب الذي خرج منه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God can return the human being to fluid as he was before.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك: إنه على رد الإنسان ماء كما كان من قبل لقادر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r4.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān says God can return a person from old age to youth, youth to childhood, and childhood to semen.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: [إن شاء رده] (2) من الكبر إلى الشباب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says God can withhold the fluid so that it does not emerge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إنه على حبس ذلك الماء لقادر حتى لا يخرج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r6.claim: Qatāda interprets the return as resurrection; Baghawī prefers this view because the following verse refers to Judgment Day and the testing of hidden deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p394#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: إن الله تعالى على بعث الإنسان وإعادته قادر وهذا أولى الأقاويل لقوله: {يوم تبلى السرائر}

BAYDAWI-FULL:86:8-9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:8-9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:8-9/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the Creator, as indicated by the earlier mention of creation.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.claim: The sūra’s purpose is to exalt the Qurʾān’s truthfulness about the reward of believers and punishment of disbelievers at Judgment, when every hidden secret is exposed and recorded.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r1.anchor: في يوم القيامة حين تبلى السرائر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.claim: The name al-Ṭāriq best signals this true promise when one reflects on the oath and the matter sworn to.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p385#s086/r3.anchor: واسمها الطارق أدل ما فيها على هذا الموعود الصادق بتأمل القسم والمقسم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r5.claim: Examining one’s beginning proves the return: whoever could originate the human can certainly resurrect it; this should make a person ensure the recording angels write only what pleases God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r5.anchor: قدر على الابتداء قدر على الإعادة قطعا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r15.speaker: الملوي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r15.claim: Al-Malawī traces the fluid from the spinal and breast regions to the testes and its successive formation every forty days into a reasoning, speaking human who can build palaces and demolish rocks; the maker can resurrect him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r15.anchor: فالذي أخرجه من ظروف عظام الصلب والترائب إلى أن صيره في محله من الأنثيين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r16.claim: After establishing preservation and the stages of human creation, the text proves resurrection, which the Arabs denied; the only difference is that re-creation is even easier.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r16.anchor: وثبت بالقدرة على ابتدائه من هذا الماء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r17.claim: Returning the human means resurrecting and restoring its original state; the phrase can also include returning the fluid to its channels and dissolving it back into fluid after it became bone, flesh, and blood.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r17.anchor: رجع الإنسان بالعبث ورده إلى حالته الأولى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r18.claim: The pronoun is more apt than naming God: each person can be asked who formed him, then told that the same all-powerful creator can restore him, whereas an explicit name might be rejected as not his creator.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r19.claim: God can reverse a person’s course from old age through adulthood, youth, childhood, embryo, clot, and drop, ultimately returning the fluid to the man’s spine and woman’s breast region.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p388/r19.anchor: رده بعد شيخوخته على عقبه بأن يجعله كهلا ثم شابا ثم طفلا ثم مضغة ثم علقة ثم نطفة

DURR-FULL:v8p475/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r4.claim: Qatada says God is able to resurrect and restore the person.
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r4.anchor: قال: إن الله على بعثه وإعادته لقادر

DURR-FULL:v8p475/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says God can make an old man young and a young man old.
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r7.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن ابن عباس في قوله: {إنه على رجعه لقادر} قال: على أن يجعل الشيخ شابا

DURR-FULL:v8p475/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r8.claim: Mujahid interprets the return as restoring the fluid to the urethra.
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r8.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر عن مجاهد {إنه على رجعه لقادر} قال: على رجع النطفة في الإحليل

DURR-FULL:v8p475/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r9.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r9.claim: Ikrima says God can return the fluid to the man’s loins.
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r9.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن عكرمة {إنه على رجعه لقادر} قال: على أن يرجعه في صلبه

DURR-FULL:v8p475/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r10.speaker: ابن أبزى
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r10.claim: Ibn Abza says God can return it as fluid to the father’s loins.
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r10.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن ابن أبزى قال: على أن يرده نطفة في صلب أبيه

DURR-FULL:v8p475/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r11.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r11.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the return as bringing the person back to life.
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن الحسن {إنه على رجعه لقادر} قال: على إحيائه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r15.claim: The pronoun in innahu refers to God.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r16.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r16.claim: Qatāda takes the pronoun in rajʿihi to refer to the human being, whom God can restore to life after death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r16.anchor: فقال قتادة وابن عباس: هو على الإنسان أي على رده حيا بعد موته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the pronoun in rajʿihi to refer to the human being, whom God can restore to life after death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r17.anchor: فقال قتادة وابن عباس: هو على الإنسان أي على رده حيا بعد موته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the human being’s resurrection after death the clearest interpretation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r19.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r19.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the human being is returned as fluid, as he was at first.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r19.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو عائد على الإنسان لكن المعنى يرجعه ماء كما كان أولا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r20.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r20.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also says God returns a person from old age to youth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r20.anchor: وقال الضحاك أيضا: يرد من الكبر إلى الشباب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r21.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r21.claim: ʿIkrima takes the pronoun to refer to the fluid, which God returns to the urethra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r21.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومجاهد: هو عائد على الماء، أي يرده في الإحليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r22.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r22.claim: Mujāhid takes the pronoun to refer to the fluid, which God returns to the urethra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r22.anchor: وقال عكرمة ومجاهد: هو عائد على الماء، أي يرده في الإحليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r23.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p465#2/r23.claim: A further view says the fluid is returned to the backbone.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r1.claim: The pronoun in inna-hu refers to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى إنه الهاء كناية عن الله عز وجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r2.claim: Rajaʿ is the return of something to its original state.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r2.anchor: الرجع رد الشيء إلى أول حاله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r3.claim: One view takes the pronoun to refer to the human: God can bring him back to life after death; al-Zajjāj links this reading to 86:9.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه على إعادة الإنسان حيا بعد موته قادر قاله الحسن وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r4.claim: A second human-related view is that God can return him through the stages from old age to youth, childhood, and semen.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه على رجعه من حال الكبر الى الشباب ومن الشباب إلى الصبأ ومن الصبأ إلى النطفة قادر قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r5.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to the water: God can return it to the urethra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r5.anchor: والقول الثاني أنها تعود إلى الماء ثم في معنى الكلام ثلاثة أقوال أحدها رد الماء في الإحليل قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r6.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r6.claim: A second water-related view is that God can return the water to the loins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r6.anchor: والثاني على رده في الصلب قاله عكرمة والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r7.claim: A third water-related view is that God can hold the water back so it does not emerge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p83/r7.anchor: والثالث على حبس الماء فلا يخرج قاله ابن زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375#2/r1.claim: Mujahid and ʿIkrima interpret the return as God’s ability to return the spurting fluid to the place from which it came.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: على رجع هذا الماء الدافق إلى مقره الذي خرج منه لقادر على ذلك. قاله مجاهد، وعكرمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the return as the resurrection of the human being made from that fluid; Ibn Jarīr prefers this reading, since the One who began creation can restore it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p375#2/r2.anchor: وهذا القول قال به الضحاك، واختاره ابن جرير

JISHUMI:v10p7367/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r8.claim: God’s power to return the human establishes resurrection and the disclosure of hidden secrets.
JISHUMI:v10p7367/r8.anchor: ويدل قوله: (إنه على رجعه لقادر) على الإعادة، وما يظهر من الأسرار.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in inna-hu refers to the Creator, indicated by the earlier mention of creation.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r2.claim: The Creator who first made the human from a drop is plainly able to recreate him; doing so presents no difficulty or incapacity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r2.anchor: على إعادته خصوصا { لقادر } لبين القدرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r3.claim: Other construals take the return as return to the point of emergence from the loins, the urethra, or the original state; on these readings the day phrase takes an omitted governing verb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p736#2/r3.anchor: إلى مخرجه من الصلب والترائب أو الإحليل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r7.claim: God is able to return semen to the urethra.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r7.anchor: على أن يرد المني في الإحليل , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r8.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r8.claim: God is able to return the fluid to the backbone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r8.anchor: على أن يرد الماء في الصلب , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r9.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r9.claim: God is able to return a person from old age to youth, childhood, and finally the semen stage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r9.anchor: من الصبا إلى النطفة , قاله الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r10.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r10.claim: God is able to resurrect a person alive after death.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r10.anchor: على أن يعيده حيا بعد موته , قاله الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r11.claim: Another possibility is that God can hold back the fluid so that it does not emerge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r11.anchor: على أن يحبس الماء فلا يخرج

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r12.claim: A further possibility is return to earthly life after resurrection, which disbelievers will request.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p247/r12.anchor: على أن يعيده إلى الدنيا بعد بعثه في الآخرة لأن الكفار يسألون الله فيها الرجعة

MUJAHID:v2p749#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p749#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p749#3/r1.claim: Mujahid interprets the return as the return of semen into the urethra, which God is able to do.
MUJAHID:v2p749#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ إنه على رجعه لقادر ﴾ قال يقول أنه لعلى رجع النطفة في الإحليل لقادر

MUQATIL:86:8-17/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:86:8-17/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:86:8-17/r1.claim: God is able to resurrect the human on the Day of Resurrection.
MUQATIL:86:8-17/r1.anchor: قادر على أن يبعثه يوم القيامة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#4/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the Creator, understood from the preceding mention of creation; the verse means the One who first created man from a drop.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#4/r1.anchor: إن الخالق لدلالة خلق عليه ومعناه ان الذى خلق الإنسان إبتداء من نظفة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#4/r2.claim: His return means bringing man back to life, and the Creator is plainly able to do so and cannot be thwarted.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#4/r2.anchor: على إعادته خصوصا ﴿ لقادر ﴾ لبين القدرة

QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r1.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r1.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak say God can return the fluid to the urethra.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r1.anchor: { إنه } أي إن الله جل ثناؤه { على رجعه } أي على رد الماء في الإحليل، { لقادر } كذا قال مجاهد والضحاك

QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r2.claim: A second view from Mujahid and al-Dahhak, also attributed to Ikrima, is that God can return the fluid to the backbone.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r2.anchor: وعنهما أيضا أن المعنى: إنه على رد الماء في الصلب وقاله عكرمة

QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r3.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak also says God can return the human to fluid, as he was before.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r3.anchor: وعن الضحاك أيضا أن المعنى: إنه على رد الإنسان ماء كما كان لقادر

QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r4.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak also interprets the return as God's ability to move a person from old age back to youth and from youth to old age; al-Mahdawi gives the same account.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r4.anchor: وعنه أيضا أن المعنى: إنه على رد الإنسان من الكبر إلى الشباب، ومن الشباب إلى الكبر، لقادر. وكذا في المهدوي

QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r5.speaker: الماوردي والثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r5.claim: Al-Mawardi and al-Tha'labi give another sequence: return from old age to childhood, and from childhood to the sperm stage.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r5.anchor: وفي الماوردي والثعلبي: إلى الصبا، ومن الصبا إلى النطفة

QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says God can withhold the fluid so that it does not emerge.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: إنه على حبس ذلك الماء حتى لا يخرج، لقادر

QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والحسن وعكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, al-Hasan, and Ikrima say God can return the person after death; al-Tabari chooses this view, and al-Tha'labi calls it strongest because of the following verse about secrets being exposed.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة والحسن وعكرمة أيضا: إنه على رد الإنسان بعد الموت لقادر

QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r8.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r8.claim: Al-Mawardi allows that God will return the person to worldly life after resurrection, as unbelievers ask God for a return.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:8/r8.anchor: قال الماوردي: ويحتمل أنه على أن يعيده إلى الدنيا بعد بعثه في الآخرة لأن الكفار يسألون الله تعالى فيها الرجعة

QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to God, who originated the human and cared for him.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r1.anchor: الله الذي أنشأه ورعاه - إنه لقادر على رجعه إلى الحياة بعد الموت

QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r2.claim: God can restore the human to life after death and renew him after decay.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r2.anchor: لقادر على رجعه إلى الحياة بعد الموت ،  وإلى التجدد بعد البلى

QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r3.claim: The first creation testifies both to God's power to restore life and to his determination and governance.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:8/r3.anchor: تشهد النشأة الأولى بقدرته ، كما تشهد بتقديره وتدبيره
